reason: The cited evidence (E1, E2) does not directly test or discuss the effect of partially substituting Hf with Ti on density or mechanical properties. E1 focuses on deformation mechanisms in a different context, and E2 describes a subtraction method on a related alloy system but provides no data on the specific Hf-Ti substitution proposed. The key premises about density reduction and retained strength are therefore unsupported by the provided passages.
premises: Hf is a heavy element that substantially contributes to density
Ti is a lighter element that maintains BCC structure and solid-solution strengthening
Partial substitution of Hf with Ti reduces average atomic mass and thus density
Key deformation mechanisms (dislocation movement in distorted lattice) remain active after substitution
The modified alloy retains comparable yield strength and ductility at room temperature and ~1000 °C
